title: A day-of-the-following-month term reaches QuickBooks as date-driven
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the test organization is connected to a QuickBooks Online sandbox company, and you can sign in to that company in another tab.
  • Create a new term of the shop's own for this test, term A, due on day 10 of the following month (it is not yet in QuickBooks).
  • Create work order 1 and work order 2 for this test, both complete, for one customer who holds term A.
custom_steps:
1. On work order 1's Finance tab, set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  2. Click Create Invoice.
  3. On work order 2's Finance tab, set Invoice Date to Oct 28, 2026.
  4. Click Create Invoice.
  5. Wait until both invoices have synced to QuickBooks.
  6. In QuickBooks, open the Terms list (Settings, All lists, Terms).
  7. In QuickBooks, open work order 1's invoice.
  8. In QuickBooks, open work order 2's invoice.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Due date reads Nov 10, 2026.

Step 2:

  • The invoice is created.

Step 3:

  • The Due date reads Nov 10, 2026.

Step 4:

  • The invoice is created.

Step 5:

  • Neither invoice is on the QB Unexported report.

Step 6:

  • Term A exists as a date-driven term, due on day 10 of the following month.

Step 7:

  • It reads terms term A and due Nov 10, 2026, matching ShopView.

Step 8:

  • It reads terms term A and due Nov 10, 2026, matching ShopView.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11677 (Story 8, QuickBooks sync - credit terms)

  • S8-R3: “A "Due day of the following month" term is created in QuickBooks as a date-driven term due on day X of the following month, so QuickBooks dates an invoice dated Oct 5 or Oct 28 with day 10 as due Nov 10, matching ShopView.”
  • S8-R1: “When a record is sent to QuickBooks with a term QuickBooks does not have, ShopView first creates the term in QuickBooks under the same name, then sends the record. This is how the standard terms already work today.”
